pointers.sentence: Around an ordinary view the wrapper calls the test with `HttpRequest.user`, through `async_to_sync` if the test is a coroutine function; such a test runs in an event loop, where reading a user not yet loaded can query the database, which Django refuses with `SynchronousOnlyOperation` (`django/utils/asyncio.py:async_unsafe`).
A true answer calls the view, a false one returns the redirect, and an exception the test raises goes out through the wrapper (`django/contrib/auth/decorators.py:user_passes_test`).

The address to come back to is the request's whole URL, from `HttpRequest.build_absolute_uri`, cut to its path and query string by `HttpRequest.get_full_path` when the login URL has no scheme or the request's, and no host or the request's (`django/contrib/auth/decorators.py:user_passes_test`).

`login_required` is `user_passes_test` with a test that reads the user's `is_authenticated`, written bare above a view or called with a login URL and a field's name; it does not look at `is_active` (`django/contrib/auth/decorators.py:login_required`).
It sets the view's attribute `"login_required"` to false and returns the same function (`django/contrib/auth/decorators.py:login_not_required`).

When the answer is no, the test raises `PermissionDenied` if the decorator was given `raise_exception=True`, which the handler turns into a 403 ([How an exception becomes a response](../handlers/exceptions.md)); otherwise it returns false, and the user is sent to the login page, logged in or not (`django/contrib/auth/decorators.py:permission_required`).

The documentation's remedy is `login_required` written above the raising decorator, which also avoids a loop when `LoginView.redirect_authenticated_user` sends a logged-in user back (`docs/topics/auth/default.txt`).
`UserPassesTestMixin.dispatch` calls, with no argument, the method `UserPassesTestMixin.get_test_func` returns, `UserPassesTestMixin.test_func` by default (`django/contrib/auth/mixins.py`).

Only an anonymous user is redirected, to an address worked out as the decorator's is; `AccessMixin.get_login_url` raises `ImproperlyConfigured` when neither `AccessMixin.login_url` nor `LOGIN_URL` gives a URL (`django/contrib/auth/mixins.py:AccessMixin.handle_no_permission`).

`LoginRequiredMiddleware.handle_no_permission` works the redirect out as the decorator does, from the view's `"login_url"` or `LOGIN_URL` (with neither, `LoginRequiredMiddleware.get_login_url` raises `ImproperlyConfigured`), and the view's `"redirect_field_name"` or `LoginRequiredMiddleware.redirect_field_name`, `"next"` (`django/contrib/auth/middleware.py:LoginRequiredMiddleware`).
5.1's release notes say the middleware does not support setting either through `LoginRequiredMixin` (`docs/releases/5.1.txt`).

A class-based view is marked through `method_decorator` on `dispatch`, which copies onto `dispatch` the attributes its decorator sets, and `View.as_view` copies those onto the function it returns (`django/utils/decorators.py:_update_method_wrapper`, `django/views/generic/base.py:View.as_view`).

So `LoginView` and the four views of the password reset are `login_not_required`; `LogoutView` is not, and the password-change views carry `login_required` (`django/contrib/auth/views.py`).

The admin marks its login view, and gives the site-wide views that `AdminSite.get_urls` wraps its login page as their login URL ([The admin](../admin.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.login`, `django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.get_urls`).

`AuthConfig.ready` registers `check_middleware`, which reports `"auth.E013"` when `LoginRequiredMiddleware` or a subclass is in `MIDDLEWARE` and `AuthenticationMiddleware` is missing or comes after it ([The system checks](../commands/checks.md)) (`django/contrib/auth/checks.py:check_middleware`).
